definition: A point in a loss landscape that is a local minimum along some directions and a local maximum along others, rather than a true minimum or maximum.
details: Saddle points are now understood to be far more common than poor local minima in the high-dimensional loss landscapes of deep neural networks, and can slow down gradient-based optimization even though they aren't true minima.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. And that is Saddle Point — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
